field theory will be Lorentzian and involve real times
t
, but upon dimensional reduction to quantum mechanics, we eventually rotate
t\to it
to match more common conventions. However, we continue to use the symbol
t
rather than
\tau
in this context for simplicity.
sending
t\to it
, so that the supercovariant derivatives are

\displaystyle D_{\pm}=\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta^{\pm}}-i\theta^{\pm}\partial_{t}\,.

(8)

Next, we perform the change of variables

\displaystyle\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\theta^{+}-i\theta^{-}\right)\,,\qquad\bar{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\theta^{+}+i\theta^{-}\right)\,,

(9)

so that

\displaystyle D=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(D_{+}+iD_{-}\right)=\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}-i\bar{\theta}\partial_{t}\,,\quad\bar{D}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(D_{+}-iD_{-}\right)=\frac{\partial}{\partial\bar{\theta}}-i\theta\partial_{t}\,.

(10)

The new supercovariant derivatives satisfy the canonical algebra

\displaystyle\{D,\bar{D}\}=-2i\partial_{t}\,,

(11)

with
D^{2}=\bar{D}^{2}=0
.

The rotation from real to complex Grassmann coordinates will introduce a factor of
i
in the measure since

\displaystyle d\theta\,d\bar{\theta}=i\,d\theta^{+}\,d\theta^{-}\,,

(12)

but this is compensated by the factor of
i
arising from the Wick rotation
dt\to i\,dt
.

Finally, in section
6
, we briefly discuss the
\mathcal{N}=1
version of our deformation.

In
\mathcal{N}=1
superspace we have a single anticommuting coordinate
\theta
, along with a corresponding supercovariant derivative

\displaystyle D=\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}-i\theta\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\,,

(13)

which satisfies the algebra

\displaystyle\{D,D\}=-2i\partial_{t}\,.

(14)

Appendix 9.B
Change of coordinates to complex supercharges

In this appendix, we carry out the change of variables to express our SUSY-QM deformation
f(\mathcal{Q}_{+},\mathcal{Q}_{-})
of (
81
) in complex coordinates, ultimately arriving at the expression (
82
) for
f(\mathcal{Q},\bar{\mathcal{Q}})
. This is a straightforward application of the change of variables described in equations (
9
) - (
11
) of appendix
9.A
, but because it involves some on-shell manipulations, we have moved the calculation to this appendix to avoid cluttering the main body.

We shift to complex supercovariant derivatives via

\displaystyle D=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(D_{+}+iD_{-}\right)\,,\quad\bar{D}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(D_{+}-iD_{-}\right)\,,

(15)

and similarly rotate the supercurrents via

\displaystyle\mathcal{Q}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\mathcal{Q}_{-}+i\mathcal{Q}_{+}\right)\,,\quad\bar{\mathcal{Q}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\mathcal{Q}_{-}-i\mathcal{Q}_{+}\right)\,.

(16)

Note that since
\mathcal{Q}_{\pm}
are fermionic, one has

\displaystyle\mathcal{Q}\bar{\mathcal{Q}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathcal{Q}_{-}^{2}-i\mathcal{Q}_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{+}+i\mathcal{Q}_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{-}+\mathcal{Q}_{+}^{2}\right)

\displaystyle=i\mathcal{Q}_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{-}\,.

(17)

Next, we compute the supercovariant derivatives. The combination
\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}
is

\displaystyle\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(D_{+}-iD_{-}\right)\left(\mathcal{Q}_{-}+i\mathcal{Q}_{+}\right)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\Big[D_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{-}+iD_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}-iD_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{-}+D_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{+}\Big]\,,

(18)

or after using the conservation equation
D_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{-}+D_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{+}=0
and the on-shell condition that
D_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}=-D_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{-}
,

\displaystyle\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}=iD_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}\,.

(19)

Likewise,

\displaystyle D\bar{\mathcal{Q}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(D_{+}+iD_{-}\right)\left(\mathcal{Q}_{-}-i\mathcal{Q}_{+}\right)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(D_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{-}-iD_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}+iD_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{-}+D_{-}\mathcal{Q}_{+}\right)\,,

(20)

and, again, this can be written on-shell as

\displaystyle D\bar{\mathcal{Q}}=-iD_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}.

(21)

Thus, we see that the new complex supercurrents satisfy the conservation equation
\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}+D\bar{\mathcal{Q}}=0
, since

\displaystyle\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}+D\bar{\mathcal{Q}}=iD_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}-iD_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}=0

(22)

when the equations of motion are satisfied.

We now return to the expression
f(\mathcal{Q}_{+},\mathcal{Q}_{-})
defining our deformation, which can now be written in terms of complex coordinates as

\displaystyle\int\,dt\,d\theta^{+}\,d\theta^{-}\,\frac{\mathcal{Q}_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{-}}{4\lambda D_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}+1}=\int\,dt\,d\theta^{+}\,d\theta^{-}\,\frac{-i\mathcal{Q}\bar{\mathcal{Q}}}{-4i\lambda\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}+1}\,.

(23)

We would now like to eliminate the factors of
i
that have appeared in (
23
). One factor arises from the change of measure via
d\theta\,d\bar{\theta}=i\,d\theta^{+}\,d\theta^{-}
. A second factor arises because, as pointed out in the discussion below (
95
), there is a relative factor of
i
arising between the natural expressions appearing in the Noether procedures which define
\mathcal{Q},\bar{\mathcal{Q}}
as opposed to
\mathcal{Q}_{+},\mathcal{Q}_{-}
. Therefore, to obtain an appropriate matching, we will rescale:

\displaystyle\mathcal{Q}\longrightarrow-i\mathcal{Q}\,,\qquad\bar{\mathcal{Q}}\longrightarrow-i\bar{\mathcal{Q}}\,.

(24)

After incorporating these two factors, we find

\displaystyle\int\,dt\,d\theta^{+}\,d\theta^{-}f(\mathcal{Q}_{+},\mathcal{Q}_{-})=\int\,dt\,d\theta\,d\bar{\theta}\frac{\mathcal{Q}\bar{\mathcal{Q}}}{-4\lambda\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}+1}\,.

(25)

Finally, we scale out an overall factor of
\frac{1}{2}
to write

\displaystyle f(\mathcal{Q}_{+},\mathcal{Q}_{-})

\displaystyle\sim\frac{\mathcal{Q}\bar{\mathcal{Q}}}{\frac{1}{2}-2\lambda\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}}\,

\displaystyle\equiv f(\mathcal{Q},\bar{\mathcal{Q}})\,,

(26)

where
\sim
indicates proportionality on-shell (as we have used conservation equations to relate
D_{+}\mathcal{Q}_{+}
to
\bar{D}\mathcal{Q}
). We chose to rescale by this prefactor to make the right side more closely match (
1
). This is the form quoted in (
82
).

Appendix 9.C
Dimensional reduction without trace flow equation

As we have pointed out in the main body of this thesis, the deformation (
1
) is very convenient for deforming quantum mechanical theories that descend from
2d
CFTs via dimensional reduction. However, for theories with potential, the trace flow equation (
133
) fails, and we cannot use this expression for the reduced
T\overline{T}
deformation. In this case, our only recourse is to directly study the
T\overline{T}
-deformed field theory in two dimensions, then compactify one spatial direction on a circle and truncate to the lowest Fourier mode.

In this appendix, we will obtain the Hamiltonian for such a theory by first solving the
2d
flow equation and then performing the circle compactification only at the final step. Suppose we begin with an undeformed Lagrangian

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{E}(\lambda=0,\phi)=\frac{1}{2}\partial^{\mu}\phi\partial_{\mu}\phi+V(\phi)\,,

(27)

with a positive sign on the potential because we work in Euclidean signature for now. The deformed Lagrangian at finite
\lambda
appears in equation (2.8) of
[
391
]
(see also
[
82
]
) as

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{E}(\lambda,\phi)

\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2\lambda}\left(\frac{1-2\lambda V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\right)

\displaystyle+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\sqrt{\left(\frac{1-2\lambda V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\right)^{2}+2\lambda\left(\frac{\partial^{\mu}\phi\partial_{\mu}\phi+2V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\right)}\,.

(28)

Again, here, the metric appearing in the
\partial^{\mu}\phi\partial_{\mu}\phi
contraction is
\delta^{\mu}{}_{\nu}
because we are in Euclidean signature. The prescription for rotating back to Minkowski signature is to multiply the Lagrangian by an overall minus sign, then to invert the sign on the time derivative of
\phi
, giving

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{M}(\lambda,\phi)=\frac{1}{2\lambda}\left(\frac{1-2\lambda V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\right)-\frac{1}{2\lambda}\sqrt{\left(\frac{1-2\lambda V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\right)^{2}+2\lambda\bigg(\frac{\phi^{\prime 2}-\dot{\phi}^{2}+2V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\bigg)}\,.

(29)

Here we used
\dot{\phi}=\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial t}
and
\phi^{\prime}=\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial x}
. We can study the behavior of
\mathcal{L}_{M}
in a few limits:

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{M}(\lambda\to 0,\phi)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\dot{\phi}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\phi^{\prime 2}-V(\phi),

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{M}(\lambda,\phi)\Big|_{\dot{\phi}=\phi^{\prime}=0}

\displaystyle=-\frac{V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)},

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{M}(\lambda,\phi)\Big|_{V(\phi)=0}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2\lambda}\bigg(1-\sqrt{1+2\lambda\big(\phi^{\prime 2}-\dot{\phi}^{2}\big)}\bigg)=\frac{1}{2\lambda}+\mathcal{L}_{\text{Nambu-Goto}}\,.

(30)

To write this as a Hamiltonian, we will resort to Legendre transform. The conjugate momentum to
\phi
is

\displaystyle\Pi=\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial\dot{\phi}}=\frac{\dot{\phi}}{\sqrt{1-2\lambda\left(1-\lambda V(\phi)\right)\big(\dot{\phi}^{2}-\phi^{\prime 2}\big)}}\,.

(31)

The relation (
31
) can be inverted to find

\displaystyle\dot{\phi}=\Pi\cdot\sqrt{\frac{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\phi^{\prime 2}}{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\Pi^{2}}}\,.

(32)

The Hamiltonian is then defined by the Legendre transformation

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}=\Pi\dot{\phi}-\mathcal{L}\,,

(33)

after replacing all instances of
\dot{\phi}
with
\Pi
using (
32
). This gives

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}=\phi^{\prime 2}\cdot

\displaystyle\sqrt{\frac{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\Pi^{2}}{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\phi^{\prime 2}}}+\frac{1}{2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\Pi^{2}}{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\phi^{\prime 2}}}

\displaystyle+\frac{V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}-\frac{1}{2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))}\,.

(34)

The dependence on
\Pi^{2}
is masked by the terms involving square roots. Near
\lambda=0
, (
34
) is

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}=\frac{1}{2}\Pi^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\phi^{\prime 2}+V(\phi)+\mathcal{O}(\lambda)\,,

(35)

which is the expected Hamiltonian for a scalar field with a potential.

Next, we would like to put the coordinate
x
on a circle of radius
R
, Fourier-expand the
x
-dependence of
\phi(x,t)
, and integrate the Hamiltonian
H
over the circle to obtain a quantum-mechanical Hamiltonian associated with the modes
\phi^{(n)}(t)
. We expand
\phi(x,t)
in modes as

\displaystyle\phi(x,t)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\phi^{(n)}_{c}(t)\cos\left(\frac{2\pi n}{R}\,x\right)+\phi^{(n)}_{s}(t)\sin\left(\frac{2\pi n}{R}\,x\right)\right)\,.

(36)

Inserting (
36
) into (
34
) and integrating over the circle would, in principle, leave us with a Hamiltonian for infinitely many interacting particles
\phi^{(n)}_{c}(t)
and
\phi^{(n)}_{s}
in quantum mechanics. Such an analysis seems intractable in general, so for simplicity, let us restrict to the zero-momentum sector
2
2

2

Restricting to the zero-momentum sector also allowed us to use the implicit solution (
183
) to the inviscid Burgers’ equation, which was pointed out in
[
82
]
.

\displaystyle\phi(x,t)\equiv\phi(t)\,.

(37)

This gives us a Hamiltonian

\displaystyle H=\frac{\sqrt{1+2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))\Pi^{2}}}{2\lambda\left(1-\lambda V(\phi)\right)}+\frac{V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}-\frac{1}{2\lambda(1-\lambda V(\phi))}\,.

(38)

For small
\lambda
, (
38
) looks like

\displaystyle H=\frac{1}{2}\Pi^{2}+V(\phi)+\lambda\left(V(\phi)^{2}-\frac{1}{4}\Pi^{4}\right)+\frac{1}{4}\lambda^{2}\left(4V(\phi)^{3}+\Pi^{4}V(\phi)+\Pi^{6}\right)+\mathcal{O}(\lambda^{3})\,,

(39)

The leading term is the usual Hamiltonian
H=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}+V(\phi)
if we identify
p=\Pi
,
m=1
. But this usual Hamiltonian receives an infinite series of corrections, which affect both the kinetic and potential terms (and mix them). The purely kinetic part of (
38
) reduces to

\displaystyle H\Big|_{V(\phi)=0}=\frac{-1+\sqrt{1+2\lambda\Pi^{2}}}{2\lambda}\,,

(40)

which is a
(0+1)
-dimensional analog of the Nambu-Goto action. If we alternatively set
\Pi=0
and consider the pure potential piece, from (
38
) we find

\displaystyle H\Big|_{\Pi=0}=\frac{V(\phi)}{1-\lambda V(\phi)}\,.

(41)

This looks identical to the result of deforming a pure-potential Hamiltonian by the function
f(H)=H^{2}
, rather than the more complicated operator (
1
), which is equivalent to
T\overline{T}
for theories that descend from deformations of
2d
CFTs. To be explicit, if we consider the flow equation:

\displaystyle\frac{\partial H}{\partial\lambda}=H^{2}\,,

(42)

with initial condition
H(0)=H_{0}
, then the solution is trivially

\displaystyle H(\lambda)=\frac{H_{0}}{1-\lambda H_{0}}\,.

(43)

At low momentum, where the kinetic term can be neglected, and the undeformed Hamiltonian is approximately the pure potential
H=V(\phi)
, this is (
41
). In particular, the Hamiltonian diverges when
V(\phi)=\frac{1}{\lambda}
. This is purely a classical statement about the solution to an
f(H)
-type flow equation, which is not necessarily indicative of the structure of the quantum theory.

However, the possible presence of poles is interesting and hints at a modification of the vacuum structure of the theory. For the moment, we will allow ourselves to speculate about the physical implications of the existence of such poles if, indeed, they persist at the quantum level.

We mention a few explicit potentials by way of examples. For instance, suppose we begin with the harmonic oscillator potential
V_{0}(\phi)=m^{2}\phi^{2}
, where we take
m=1
for simplicity. The potential deforms as follows:

\displaystyle\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=137.9979pt]{diagrams/phi_square.pdf}}\longrightarrow\;\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=137.9979pt]{diagrams/deformed_phisquare.pdf}}

(44)

It is very natural to ask what has happened to the basis of eigenfunctions after applying this deformation. The undeformed potential is the usual harmonic oscillator, whose eigenstates are Hermite polynomials. However, the deformed potential has infinite barriers at
\phi=\pm 1
. One might believe that there is a complete set of eigenfunctions for the deformed potential, which are forced to vanish at
\phi=\pm 1
. The regions
|\phi|>1
seem to have been “cut off” from the theory by applying this deformation.

Another interesting case to consider is a linear potential
V(\phi)=\phi
.

\displaystyle\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=137.9979pt]{diagrams/phi_linear.pdf}}\longrightarrow\;\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=137.9979pt]{diagrams/deformed_philinear.pdf}}

(45)

Now, the change is even more drastic: the undeformed linear potential had eigenstates, which were Airy functions, but they were non-normalizable because the potential was unbounded below. The deformation has now inserted a hard cutoff at
\phi=1
. To the left of this cutoff, the potential is bounded below as
V(\phi)>-1
. Has the
T\overline{T}
deformation “cured” the non-normalizability of the linear potential? If so, is there a relationship between the undeformed eigenstates (Airy functions) and the eigenstates of the deformed potential?

For a third example, the double-well potential
V(\phi)=\left(1-\phi^{2}\right)^{2}
deforms as

\displaystyle\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=137.9979pt]{diagrams/double_well.pdf}}\longrightarrow\;\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=137.9979pt]{diagrams/double_well_deformed.pdf}}

(46)

Now, there is a pole at
\phi=0
, so the two wells have become separated by an infinite potential barrier. Again, one might wonder what has happened to the Hilbert space. Is there still a complete basis of eigenfunctions, but now localized to each of the disconnected wells?

The above examples are presented only in the context of ordinary quantum mechanics without any supersymmetry. However, one might hope that the presence of some SUSY might be useful in learning about the fate of the Hilbert space after such a deformation. For instance, the spectrum of ground states in a supersymmetric theory exhibits a great deal of structure, and one can extract data about it using index-like quantities. Is there some calculation in SUSY-QM theory that is sensitive to the fact that the two ground states in the double well (
46
) may have been “cut off” from one another in the deformed theory? It would be exciting to gain a better understanding of the Hilbert space of these deformed quantum mechanics theories and to understand whether
T\overline{T}
or
f(\mathcal{Q},\bar{\mathcal{Q}})
indeed has effects on the infrared structure of the kind described here.

Chapter 10
AdS
3
with
T\overline{T}
-Deformed Boundary Conditions

In section
4
, we used several methods that have been developed for studying
\mathrm{AdS}_{3}
gravity with
T\overline{T}
-deformed boundary conditions, both in the metric formalism
[
109
]
and in the Chern-Simons formalism
[
112
]
. To make the present work self-contained, we review some aspects of these methods in this appendix, which are also useful for our analysis of root-
T\overline{T}
deformed boundary conditions. We refer the reader to the original works for further details and to the related work
[
110
]
for additional results in the Chern-Simons formalism.

Appendix 10.A
Metric formalism

We recall that the modified metric
\gamma_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}
and stress tensor
T_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}
corresponding to a boundary
T\overline{T}
deformation satisfy (
48
) which was re-derived in the main text. By equating the coefficients of the independent terms on both sides of this equation, one arrives at a set of partial differential equations for the deformed quantities. These differential equations were first analyzed in
[
392
]
, where it was shown that they can be written as

\frac{\partial\gamma_{\alpha\beta}}{\partial\lambda}=-2\hat{T}_{\alpha\beta}\,,\quad\frac{\partial\hat{T}_{\alpha\beta}}{\partial\lambda}=-\hat{T}_{\alpha\gamma}\hat{T}_{\beta}{}^{\gamma}\,,\quad\frac{\partial(\hat{T}_{\alpha\gamma}\hat{T}_{\beta}{}^{\gamma})}{\partial\lambda}=0\,.

(1)

Here we have omitted the
(\lambda)
superscripts on
\gamma_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}
and
\widehat{T}_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}=T_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}-\gamma_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}T^{(\lambda)\rho}{}_{\rho}
.

The solutions of (
1
) are (
6
). In terms of the Fefferman-Graham quantities, the deformed boundary metric and stress tensor are

\displaystyle\gamma^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}

\displaystyle=g^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}-\frac{2\lambda}{8\pi G\ell}g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}+\frac{\lambda^{2}}{\left(8\pi G\ell\right)^{2}}g^{(2)}_{\alpha\rho}g^{(2)}_{\sigma\beta}\gamma^{(0)\rho\sigma}

(2)

\displaystyle=g^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}-\lambda g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}+\lambda^{2}g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}\,,

and

\displaystyle\widehat{T}^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}

\displaystyle=\widehat{T}^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}-\lambda\widehat{T}^{(0)}_{\alpha\rho}\,\widehat{T}^{(0)}_{\sigma\beta}\gamma^{(0)\rho\sigma}

(3)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8\pi G\ell}g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}-\frac{\lambda}{(8\pi G\ell)^{2}}g^{(2)}_{\alpha\rho}g^{(2)}_{\sigma\beta}g^{(0)\rho\sigma}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}-2\lambda g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}\right)\,,

where we used (
125
) and work in conventions such that
4\pi G\ell=1
. For the bad sign of the deformation parameter, these modified asymptotic boundary conditions can be interpreted as Dirichlet boundary conditions at a finite radial coordinate
\rho_{c}=-\frac{\lambda}{4\pi G\ell}
.
1
1

1

One can see by straightforward algebra that the asymptotic conditions (
2
) are equivalent to fixing the induced metric to be
g_{\alpha\beta}^{(0)}
at this value of
\rho_{c}
if
\lambda<0
. Another way to determine the relation between the bulk cutoff
\rho_{c}
and the
T\overline{T}
coupling
\lambda
is using the trace flow equation
T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha}\propto\lambda\det T_{\alpha\beta}

[
108
,
88
,
118
]
.

Although we are primarily interested in the good sign of the deformation, it is convenient to express various quantities in terms of
\rho_{c}
. We have
\rho_{c}<0
, and in this context,
\rho_{c}
cannot be interpreted as a physical value of the coordinate
\rho
. Thus

\gamma^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}=g^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}+\rho_{c}g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}+\rho_{c}^{2}g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}\,,\quad\widehat{T}^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}=\frac{1}{2}\left(g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}+2\rho_{c}g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}\right)\,.

(4)

Specializing to a Bañados geometry (
129
), the boundary metric in Fefferman-Graham quantities is

\gamma^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}=du\,dv+\rho_{c}\left(\mathcal{L}(u)du^{2}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dv^{2}\right)+\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)du\,dv\,.

(5)

We express (
5
) as

\gamma^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}=dU\,dV\,,

(6)

where
(U,V)
are the undeformed coordinates

dU=du+\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dv,\quad dV=dv+\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)du\,.

(7)

In matrix form, we can define the state-dependent coordinate transformation in (
7
) and its inverse as

\displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{c}dU\\
dV\end{array}\right)

\displaystyle=\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}1&\quad\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)\\
\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)&\quad 1\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}[]{c}du\\
dv\end{array}\right),

(8)

\displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{c}du\\
dv\end{array}\right)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}1&\quad-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)\\
-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)&\quad 1\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}[]{c}dU\\
dV\end{array}\right)\,.

Using (
8
), we can write the boundary metric
g^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}
in the
(U,V)
coordinates

\displaystyle g^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}

\displaystyle=du\,dv

(9)

\displaystyle=\frac{(dU-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dV)(dV-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)dU)}{(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))^{2}}\,,

as well as the other Fefferman-Graham quantities:

\displaystyle g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}(u)du^{2}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dv^{2}

(10)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}(u)\left(\frac{dU-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)}\right)^{2}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)\left(\frac{dV-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(v)}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)}\right)^{2}

\displaystyle=\frac{(1+\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))(\mathcal{L}(u)dU^{2}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}dV^{2})-4\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dU\,dV}{(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))^{2}}\,,

and

\displaystyle g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)du\,dv

(11)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)\frac{(dU-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dV)(dV-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)dU)}{(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))^{2}}\,.

Proving (
11
) is straightforward:

\displaystyle g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}g^{(2)}_{\alpha\rho}g^{(2)}_{\sigma\beta}g^{(0)\rho\sigma}

(12)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}\mathcal{L}(u)&\quad 0\\
0&\quad\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}0&\quad 2\\
2&\quad 0\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}\mathcal{L}(u)&\quad 0\\
0&\quad\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)\end{array}\right)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)g^{(0)}_{\alpha\beta}\,.

Substituting the expressions for
g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}
and
g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}
in (
10
) and (
11
) into the result (
4
) for the trace-reversed deformed stress tensor
\widehat{T}^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}
, we find that

\displaystyle\widehat{T}^{(\lambda)}_{\alpha\beta}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(g^{(2)}_{\alpha\beta}+2\rho_{c}g^{(4)}_{\alpha\beta}\right)dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}

(13)

\displaystyle=\frac{\mathcal{L}(u)dU^{2}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dV^{2}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dU\,dV}{2(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))}\,,

and trace-reversing to obtain the deformed stress tensor in the
(U,V)
coordinates yields

T_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}=\frac{\mathcal{L}(u)dU^{2}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dV^{2}+2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v)dU\,dV}{2(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}(u)\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))}\,.

(14)

It is straightforward to show that (
14
) obeys the
T\overline{T}
trace flow equation and is conserved:

\partial_{V}T^{(\lambda)}_{UU}+\partial_{U}T^{(\lambda)}_{VU}=\partial_{V}T^{(\lambda)}_{UV}+\partial_{U}T^{(\lambda)}_{VV}=0\,.

(15)

From this Fefferman-Graham analysis, we have therefore determined the deformed black hole solutions for constant
(\mathcal{L}(u),\bar{\mathcal{L}}(v))\equiv(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda},\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})
. In terms of the temporal and angular coordinates
\phi
and
T
, (
14
) becomes

\displaystyle T_{\alpha\beta}^{(\lambda)}dx^{\alpha}\,dx^{\beta}

(16)

\displaystyle=\frac{(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})dT^{2}+(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}+2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})d\phi^{2}+2(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})d\phi\,dT}{2(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})}\,,

where
(U,V)=(\phi+T,\phi-T)
. Therefore, in the
(T,\phi)
coordinates and restoring factors of
4\pi G\ell
, we find that the deformed energy and angular momentum are

\displaystyle E_{\lambda}

\displaystyle=\int^{R}_{0}d\phi~T^{(\lambda)}_{TT}=\frac{R(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})}{8\pi G\ell(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})}\,,

(17)

\displaystyle J_{\lambda}

\displaystyle=\int^{R}_{0}d\phi~T^{(\lambda)}_{T\phi}=\frac{R(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})}{8\pi G\ell(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})}\,.

The functions
(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda},\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})
are fixed in terms of
(\mathcal{L}_{0},\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0})
by equating the undeformed and deformed angular momenta and event horizon areas
[
109
]
. This is possible because the
T\overline{T}
flow preserves the boundary theory’s degeneracy of states, which implies that the horizon area of the black hole is unchanged by the deformation. The angular momentum is holographically dual to the momentum
P_{n}
of the state in the field theory, which is quantized in units of
\frac{1}{R}
and thus cannot flow with the deformation parameter because
\lambda
is continuous. We expect that these two assumptions should hold for
any
stress tensor deformation of the boundary field theory (including root-
T\overline{T}
) since any flow equation for the spectrum, which is driven by a function of only energies and momenta will also preserve degeneracies.

We have already determined the angular momentum, so we now consider the horizon areas. The event horizon in the Fefferman-Graham gauge is at

\rho_{h}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{0}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}}\,,

(18)

and (
129
) evaluated at (
18
) is

\displaystyle ds^{2}|_{\rho_{h}=(\mathcal{L}_{0}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0})^{-\frac{1}{2}}}=\frac{\ell^{2}\mathcal{L}_{0}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}{4}d\rho^{2}

(19)

\displaystyle+\left(\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{0}}-\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}\right)^{2}dT^{2}+\left(\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{0}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}\right)^{2}d\phi^{2}+2\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)dTd\phi\,.

For the deformed black hole metric, substituting (
9
) - (
11
) into (
129
) evaluated at the event horizon

\rho_{h}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}\,,

(20)

we obtain

\displaystyle ds^{2}|_{\rho_{h}=(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})^{-\frac{1}{2}}}

\displaystyle=\frac{\ell^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{4}d\rho^{2}

(21)

\displaystyle+\frac{\left(\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}-\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)^{2}dT^{2}+\left(\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)^{2}d\phi^{2}+2(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})d\phi dT}{\left(1+\rho_{c}\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)^{2}}\,,

which has an event horizon area

A^{(\lambda)}=\int^{R}_{0}d\phi\sqrt{g_{\phi\phi}}|_{\rho_{h}=(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})^{-\frac{1}{2}}}=R\frac{\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}{1+\rho_{c}\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}\,.

(22)

Equating the undeformed and deformed event horizon areas and angular momenta, we arrive at the constraints for
(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda},\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})
,

\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{0}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}=\frac{\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}{1+\rho_{c}\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}},\quad\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}=\frac{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\,.

(23)

The solution to (
23
) is

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}

\displaystyle=\resizebox{18088005}{}{$\frac{-\left(1+\rho_{c}(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0})\right)\sqrt{\rho_{c}^{2}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)^{2}-2\rho_{c}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)+1}+\rho_{c}^{2}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)^{2}-2\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}+1}{2\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{0}},$}

(24)

\displaystyle\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}

\displaystyle=\resizebox{18088005}{}{$\frac{-\left(1-\rho_{c}(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0})\right)\sqrt{\rho_{c}^{2}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)^{2}-2\rho_{c}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)+1}+\rho_{c}^{2}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)^{2}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{0}+1}{2\rho_{c}^{2}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}\,.$}

Substituting (
24
) into the energy equation (
17
), we arrive at the well-established
T\overline{T}
-deformed energy expressed in terms of the field theory energy
E_{0}
and momentum
P_{0}
,

\displaystyle E_{\lambda}

\displaystyle=\frac{R}{8\pi G\ell\rho_{c}}\left(1-\sqrt{1-2\rho_{c}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)+\rho_{c}^{2}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)^{2}}\right)

(25)

\displaystyle=\frac{R}{2\lambda}\left(\sqrt{1+\frac{4\lambda E_{0}}{R}+\frac{4\lambda^{2}P_{0}^{2}}{R^{2}}}-1\right)\,,

where the undeformed energy
E_{0}
, angular momentum
J_{0}
(which corresponds to the momentum
P_{0}
in the CFT), and deformation parameter with units restored are

E_{0}=\frac{R}{8\pi G\ell}(\mathcal{L}_{0}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0})\,,\quad J_{0}=\frac{R}{8\pi G\ell}\left(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}\right)=P_{0}\,,\quad\lambda=-4\pi G\ell\rho_{c}\,.

(26)

Appendix 10.B
Chern-Simons formalism

To obtain the
T\overline{T}
-deformed Chern-Simons connections, we use the coordinate transformation in (
8
) to obtain

\displaystyle A(\rho_{c})

\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2\rho}L_{0}d\rho+\frac{1}{\ell}\left(-\sqrt{\rho}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}L_{-1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}L_{1}\right)\left(\frac{dU-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}dV}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)\,,

(27)

\displaystyle\bar{A}(\rho_{c})

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2\rho}L_{0}d\rho+\frac{1}{\ell}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}L_{-1}-\sqrt{\rho}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}L_{1}\right)\left(\frac{dV-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}dU}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)\,.

We can see that the deformed gauge fields obey a mixed boundary condition:

\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}A_{U}(\rho_{c})+A_{V}(\rho_{c})=0\,,\quad\bar{A}_{U}(\rho_{c})+\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{A}_{V}(\rho_{c})=0\,.

(28)

To convert the connections from the
(U,V)
coordinates to the
(T,\phi)
coordinates, we recall that

\displaystyle A

\displaystyle=A_{\alpha}dx^{\alpha}

(29)

\displaystyle=A_{U}dU+A_{V}dV

\displaystyle=\left(A_{U}+A_{V}\right)d\phi+\left(A_{U}-A_{V}\right)dT\,,

yielding

\displaystyle A_{\phi}=A_{U}+A_{V},\quad A_{T}=A_{U}-A_{V}\,,\quad\bar{A}_{\phi}=\bar{A}_{U}+\bar{A}_{V}\,,\quad\bar{A}_{T}=\bar{A}_{U}-\bar{A}_{V}\,.

(30)

Hence

A_{\phi}(\rho_{c})=\frac{1}{\ell}\frac{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\left(-\sqrt{\rho}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}L_{-1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}L_{1}\right)\,,\quad A_{T}(\rho_{c})=\frac{1+\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}A_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\,,

(31)

and

\bar{A}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})=\frac{1}{\ell}\frac{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}L_{-1}-\sqrt{\rho}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}L_{1}\right)\,,\quad\bar{A}_{T}(\rho_{c})=-\frac{1+\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}\bar{A}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\,.

(32)

The boundary connections obey a similar relation as the bulk connections

\displaystyle a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})=\frac{1}{\ell}\frac{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\left(-\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}L_{-1}+L_{1}\right)\,,\quad a_{T}(\rho_{c})=\frac{1+\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\,,

(33)

and

\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})=\frac{1}{\ell}\frac{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\left(L_{-1}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}L_{1}\right)\,,\quad\bar{a}_{T}(\rho_{c})=-\frac{1+\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\,.

(34)

We may also study the black hole entropy and horizon areas using these deformed connections in the same way as we did in the root-
T\overline{T}
deformed case around equation (
161
). The analogs of the matrices
(\lambda_{\phi},\bar{\lambda}_{\phi})
in (
162
), which are simply the diagonalized versions of
(a_{\phi},\bar{a}_{\phi})
, for the
T\overline{T}
-deformed connections (
34
), are

\displaystyle\lambda_{\phi}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\ell}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}\frac{\left(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}&\quad 0\\
0&\quad-\frac{\left(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\end{array}\right)\,,

(35)

\displaystyle\bar{\lambda}_{\phi}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\ell}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}-\frac{\left(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\right)\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}&\quad 0\\
0&\quad\frac{\left(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\right)\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\end{array}\right)\,.

Using the equation
S=C\operatorname{Tr}\left((\lambda_{\phi}-\bar{\lambda}_{\phi})L_{0}\right)
for the entropy, which we quoted in (
161
), we find an expression for the deformed entropy
S^{(\lambda)}
:

S^{(\lambda)}=\frac{C}{\ell}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}{1+\rho_{c}\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}}\right)\,.

(36)

Setting (
36
) equal to the undeformed entropy

\displaystyle S^{(0)}=\frac{C}{\ell}\left(\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_{0}}+\sqrt{\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{0}}\right)\,,

(37)

then reproduces the area equation (
23
).

Following
[
112
]
, we can now read off the variation of the boundary action, which is compatible with the relations (
33
) and (
34
) for the deformed boundary connections:

\displaystyle\delta S=-\frac{\ell}{8\pi G}\int_{\partial M}dT\,d\phi\,

\displaystyle\Bigg(\operatorname{Tr}\left[\left(a_{T}(\rho_{c})-\frac{1+\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right)\delta a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right]

\displaystyle\qquad-\operatorname{Tr}\left[\left(\bar{a}_{T}(\rho_{c})+\frac{1+\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right)\delta\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right]\Bigg)\,.

(38)

We see that, when the constraints (
33
) and (
34
) are satisfied, the variation (
38
) collapses to
\delta S_{\text{bdry}}=0
. This guarantees a well-defined variational principle.

To determine this boundary action in terms of
\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}
,
\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}
, and
\rho_{c}
, we must first evaluate the variations of the boundary connections. The variations of (
33
) and (
34
) are

\displaystyle\delta a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})

\displaystyle=\frac{(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})\left(L_{-1}-\rho_{c}^{2}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}L_{1}\right)\delta\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-\rho_{c}\left(\mathcal{L}_{\mu}L_{-1}-L_{1}\right)\left(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\right)\delta\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{\ell\left(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)^{2}}\,,

(39)

\displaystyle\delta\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})

\displaystyle=\frac{-\rho_{c}\left(L_{-1}-\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\mu}L_{1}\right)\left(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)\delta\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-\left(\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\mu}L_{-1}-L_{1}\right)\left(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\right)\delta\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{\ell\left(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)^{2}}\,.

The variation of the boundary piece is

\displaystyle\delta S_{\text{bdry}}=\frac{\ell}{8\pi G}\int_{\partial M}dT\,d\phi

\displaystyle\bigg(\frac{1+\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\operatorname{Tr}\left(a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\delta a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right)

(40)

\displaystyle+\frac{1+\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}\operatorname{Tr}\left(\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\delta\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right)\bigg)\,,

and using (
39
), the traces evaluate to

\displaystyle\operatorname{Tr}\left(a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\delta a_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right)

\displaystyle=\resizebox{13566090}{}{$\frac{(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})^{2}(1+\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})\delta\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda})(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})\delta\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{\ell^{2}(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})^{3}}\,,$}

(41)

\displaystyle\operatorname{Tr}\left(\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\delta\bar{a}_{\phi}(\rho_{c})\right)

\displaystyle=\resizebox{13566090}{}{$\frac{-2\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda})(1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})\delta\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+(1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda})^{2}(1+\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})\delta\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{\ell^{2}(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})^{3}}\,.$}

Substituting (
41
) into (
40
), the varied boundary action in terms of
\delta\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}
and
\delta\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}
is

\delta S_{\text{bdry}}=\frac{1}{8\pi G\ell}\int_{\partial M}dT\,d\phi\left(\left(\frac{1-\rho_{c}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)^{2}\delta\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+\left(\frac{1-\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\right)^{2}\delta\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)\,,

(42)

from which
S_{\text{bdry}}
can be read off as

S_{\text{bdry}}=\frac{1}{8\pi G\ell}\int_{\partial M}dT\,d\phi\,\frac{\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}{1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}}\,.

(43)

After integration over
\phi
in (
43
), we find that

\displaystyle S_{\text{bdry}}

\displaystyle=\int\,dT\,\frac{R\left(\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}+\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}-2\rho_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda}\right)}{8\pi G\ell(1-\rho_{c}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}\bar{\mathcal{L}}_{\lambda})}\,

\displaystyle=\int\,dT\,E_{\lambda}\,,

(44)

where we have used the expression for
E_{\lambda}
in (
17
). Therefore, the boundary Lagrangian density in the Chern-Simons formalism agrees with the deformed mass (or energy) of the bulk spacetime as computed in the metric formalism.

We emphasize again that it was not clear
a priori
that the boundary Chern-Simons action would necessarily reproduce the mass of the deformed spacetime. Although this is true in the undeformed theory, after adding a boundary deformation that implements mixed boundary conditions in the bulk, one needs to compute the Hamiltonian to argue that the Chern-Simons boundary action will agree with the deformed spacetime mass in general. However, in this case, we have seen by explicit computation that the two agree, at least for the class of Bañados-type solutions we are considering.

Chapter 11
Perturbative Actions and Modified Scalar Feynman Diagrams

Appendix 11.A
Perturbative
f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})
-Deformed Actions

Throughout this paper, we have considered various deformations which are constructed from the energy-momentum tensor. Although the most important examples within this class are the
T\overline{T}
and root-
T\overline{T}
flows, it appears that
general
stress tensor deformations nonetheless have interesting properties – for instance, we have shown that every parameterized family of interacting
2d
chiral boson theories which enjoys non-manifest Lorentz invariance admits an interpretation as a stress tensor deformation. This is a
2d
analog of similar theorems about
4d
theories of duality-invariant electrodynamics
[
312
]
or
6d
chiral tensor theories
[
314
]
.

Motivated by these observations, one may wish to study
2d
deformations by other functions of the energy-momentum tensor, besides the ones considered in the body of this manuscript. One way to do this is to solve the resulting flow equations perturbatively, i.e. order-by-order in the deformation parameter. In this appendix we will use
g
for the parameter of a general stress tensor flow, which is not to be confused with the metric
g_{\alpha\beta}
or its determinant.

Let us therefore consider the following general class of operators in
2d
which can be expressed in terms of the two independent Lorentz scalars that can be built from the stress tensor, namely
\operatorname{Tr}(T)=T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha}
and
\operatorname{Tr}(T^{2})=T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta}
:

f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})\,.

(1)

We note that all higher traces of the stress tensor,
\operatorname{Tr}(T^{n})
for
n>2
, can be expressed in terms of these two lower traces. Given such an operator, we wish to study the flow equation
1
1

1

One can also consider flows driven by a function
f
which has explicit dependence on the deformation parameter
g
. For instance, the so-called
T\overline{T}+\Lambda_{2}
deformation is defined by performing a
T\overline{T}
deformation and then activating a cosmological constant proportional to
\frac{1}{\lambda}
. See
[
140
,
141
,
143
,
142
,
393
,
394
]
for further details.

\frac{\partial S^{(g)}}{\partial g}=\int d^{2}x\,E\,f(T^{\alpha}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})\,.

(2)

The solution to (
2
) can be written as a series expansion,

S^{(g)}=S^{(0)}+\sum^{\infty}_{m=1}\frac{g^{m}}{m}\int d^{2}x\,E\,f(T^{\alpha}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})_{m-1}\,,

(3)

where we write
f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})_{m}
for the term of order
g^{m}
in the expression for the
f
operator computed from the action at order
g^{m-1}
. Because each term in this expansion only depends on the data of lower-order terms, one can build up the solution iteratively in powers of
g
.

As in section
2
of the main text, we will work in the tetrad formalism with a Lorentzian tangent-space metric and with spacetime coordinates
x^{\alpha}=(t,\theta)
. A general spacetime metric can therefore be expanded in terms of vielbeins as

g_{\alpha\beta}=E^{a}{}_{\alpha}E^{b}{}_{\beta}\eta_{ab}=-\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}2E^{+}{}_{t}E^{-}{}_{t}&\quad E^{+}{}_{t}E^{-}{}_{\theta}+E^{-}{}_{t}E^{+}{}_{\theta}\\
E^{+}{}_{t}E^{-}{}_{\theta}+E^{-}{}_{t}E^{+}{}_{\theta}&\quad 2E^{+}{}_{\theta}E^{-}{}_{\theta}\end{array}\right)\,.

(4)

The stress tensor associated with a general action
S
, which has been coupled to gravity using the vielbeins
E^{a}{}_{\alpha}
, can be written as

T^{\alpha}{}_{\beta}=-\frac{1}{E}\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{a}{}_{\alpha}}E^{a}{}_{\beta}=-\frac{1}{E}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{+}{}_{t}}E^{+}{}_{t}+\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{-}{}_{t}}E^{-}{}_{t}&\quad\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{+}{}_{\theta}}E^{+}{}_{t}+\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{-}{}_{\theta}}E^{-}{}_{t}\\
\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{+}{}_{t}}E^{+}{}_{\theta}+\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{-}{}_{t}}E^{-}{}_{\theta}&\quad\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{+}{}_{\theta}}E^{+}{}_{\theta}+\frac{\partial S}{\partial E^{-}{}_{\theta}}E^{-}{}_{\theta}\end{array}\right)\,.

(5)

We will use the general expression (
5
) for the stress tensor, along with the expansion (
3
), to perturbatively solve the flow equation (
2
) for various choices of the
f
operator.

We begin by finding perturbative solutions for some of the flow equations considered in the main text, before generalizing to other deformations which were not considered in the body. In our examples, we compute the stress tensor (
5
) using the vielbein formalism due to computational speed in
Mathematica
, but we note that the metric formalism gives identical results.

Root-
T\overline{T}
Perturbative Flow for Multiple Bosons

For our first example, we will consider the perturbative solution to the root-
T\overline{T}
flow equation for an arbitrary number of non-chiral bosons
\varphi^{i}
,
i=1,\ldots,N
. This flow equation was first solved in closed-form in
[
270
]
.

We take a seed action which describes
N
free massless bosons in Lorentzian signature,

\displaystyle S^{(0)}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\int d^{2}x\sqrt{-g}g^{\alpha\beta}\partial_{\alpha}\varphi^{i}\partial_{\beta}\varphi^{i}

(6)

\displaystyle=\int d^{2}x\frac{E^{-}{}_{\theta}E^{+}{}_{\theta}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}+E^{-}{}_{t}E^{+}{}_{t}\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}-\left(E^{-}{}_{\theta}E^{+}{}_{t}+E^{-}{}_{t}E^{+}{}_{\theta}\right)\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime i}}{E}\,,

which have been coupled to gravity using the tetrad formalism. We then deform using the root-
T\overline{T}
operator, which corresponds to the general
f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})
operator of equation (
1
) being

f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})=\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta}-\frac{1}{2}\left(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha}\right)^{2}}\,.

(7)

In this case, the perturbative solution (
3
) to the flow equation takes the form

S^{(\gamma)}=S^{(0)}+\sum^{\infty}_{m=1}\frac{\gamma^{m}}{m}\int d^{2}xE~\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{m-1}\,.

(8)

Following the conventions in the main text, we use the symbol
\gamma
for the flow parameter of a root-
T\overline{T}
deformation, rather than the variable
g
which stood for the parameter in a general deformation above.

The first few terms in this perturbative expansion are

\displaystyle\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)}\,,

(9)

\displaystyle\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\,,\quad\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{2}|_{\text{flat}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}\,,\quad\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{3}|_{\text{flat}}=\frac{1}{6}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}\,,

\displaystyle\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{4}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{24}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}\,,\quad\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{5}|_{\text{flat}}=\frac{1}{120}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}\,,

where “flat” means that we have set the vielbeins to their flat-space values (
58
).

We note that the quantities appearing in (
9
) can be written in terms of the manifestly Lorentz-invariant combinations

\displaystyle\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\nu}\varphi^{i}\right)\left(\partial_{\nu}\varphi^{j}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{j}\right)

\displaystyle=\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime j}\right)

(10)

\displaystyle=(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i})^{2}+(\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i})^{2}-2(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime i})^{2}\,,

and

\displaystyle 2\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\nu}\varphi^{i}\right)\left(\partial_{\nu}\varphi^{j}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{j}\right)-\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{i}\right)^{2}

(11)

\displaystyle=\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\right)^{2}+\left(\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}\right)^{2}-4\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime i}\right)^{2}+2\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime j}\varphi^{\prime j}

\displaystyle=\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\,.

In terms of these quantities, one finds that the perturbative expansion to the flow equation converges to the solution (
230
),

\displaystyle S^{(\gamma)}=S^{(0)}+\int dt\,d\theta\,\bigg(\gamma\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}+\frac{\gamma^{2}}{2}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}+\frac{\gamma^{3}}{6}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}

(12)

\displaystyle+\frac{\gamma^{4}}{24}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}+\frac{\gamma^{5}}{120}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}+\frac{\gamma^{6}}{720}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}+\cdots\bigg)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\int dt\,d\theta\,\bigg[\partial_{\alpha}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\alpha}\varphi^{i}\left(1+\frac{\gamma^{2}}{2}+\frac{\gamma^{4}}{24}+\frac{\gamma^{6}}{720}+\mathcal{O}(\gamma^{8})\right)

\displaystyle+\sqrt{2\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\nu}\varphi^{i}\right)\left(\partial_{\nu}\varphi^{j}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{j}\right)-\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{i}\right)^{2}}\left(\gamma+\frac{\gamma^{3}}{6}+\frac{\gamma^{5}}{120}+\mathcal{O}(\gamma^{7})\right)\bigg]

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\int dt\,d\theta\,\bigg[\cosh(\gamma)\partial_{\alpha}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\alpha}\varphi^{i}

\displaystyle+\sinh(\gamma)\sqrt{2\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\nu}\varphi^{i}\right)\left(\partial_{\nu}\varphi^{j}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{j}\right)-\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{i}\right)^{2}}\bigg]\,.

Root-
T\overline{T}
Perturbative Flow for Chern-Simons

An almost identical calculation can be performed to study the perturbative root-
T\overline{T}
deformation of the Chern-Simons boundary action given in (
94
). The first few terms in the expansion are

\displaystyle\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\sqrt{\left(k^{ij}A_{iw}A_{jw}+\bar{k}^{\overline{i}\overline{j}}\bar{A}_{\overline{i}w}\bar{A}_{\overline{j}w}\right)\left(k^{mn}A_{m\bar{w}}A_{n\bar{w}}+\bar{k}^{\overline{m}\overline{n}}\bar{A}_{\overline{m}\bar{w}}\bar{A}_{\overline{n}\bar{w}}\right)}\,,

(13)

\displaystyle\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(k^{ij}A_{iw}A_{j\bar{w}}+\bar{k}^{\overline{i}\overline{j}}\bar{A}_{\overline{i}w}\bar{A}_{\overline{j}\bar{w}}\right)\,,

\displaystyle\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{2}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}\,,\quad\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{3}|_{\text{flat}}=\frac{1}{6}\mathcal{R}^{(\gamma)}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}\,,

where now “flat” means that we have set the vielbeins equal to the values (
164
) appropriate for a flat
Euclidean
tangent space metric, following the conventions of section
3
.

Therefore, the root-
T\overline{T}
-deformed Chern-Simons boundary action is

\displaystyle I^{(\gamma)}_{\partial\mathcal{M}_{3}}

(14)

\displaystyle=\frac{i}{8\pi}\int_{\partial\mathcal{M}_{3}}dwd\bar{w}\left(-\left(k^{ij}A_{iw}A_{j\bar{w}}+\bar{k}^{\overline{i}\overline{j}}\bar{A}_{\overline{i}w}\bar{A}_{\overline{j}\bar{w}}\right)\left(1+\frac{\gamma^{2}}{2}+\mathcal{O}(\gamma^{4})\right)\right)

\displaystyle+\frac{i}{8\pi}\int_{\partial\mathcal{M}_{3}}dwd\bar{w}\sqrt{\left(k^{ij}A_{iw}A_{jw}+\bar{k}^{\overline{i}\overline{j}}\bar{A}_{\overline{i}w}\bar{A}_{\overline{j}w}\right)\left(k^{mn}A_{m\bar{w}}A_{n\bar{w}}+\bar{k}^{\bar{m}\bar{n}}\bar{A}_{\bar{m}\bar{w}}\bar{A}_{\bar{n}\bar{w}}\right)}

\displaystyle\cdot\left(\gamma+\frac{\gamma^{3}}{6}+\mathcal{O}(\gamma^{5})\right)

\displaystyle=\frac{i}{8\pi}\int_{\partial\mathcal{M}_{3}}dwd\bar{w}\bigg[-\cosh(\gamma)\left(k^{ij}A_{iw}A_{j\bar{w}}+\bar{k}^{\overline{i}\overline{j}}\bar{A}_{\overline{i}w}\bar{A}_{\overline{j}\bar{w}}\right)

\displaystyle+\sinh(\gamma)\sqrt{\left(k^{ij}A_{iw}A_{jw}+\bar{k}^{\overline{i}\overline{j}}\bar{A}_{\overline{i}w}\bar{A}_{\overline{j}w}\right)\left(k^{mn}A_{m\bar{w}}A_{n\bar{w}}+\bar{k}^{\bar{m}\bar{n}}\bar{A}_{\bar{m}\bar{w}}\bar{A}_{\bar{n}\bar{w}}\right)}\bigg]\,.

T\overline{T}
Perturbative Flow for a Single Boson

For our next example, we will consider the irrelevant
T\overline{T}
flow rather than the marginal root-
T\overline{T}
flow. For simplicity, we will restrict to a deformation of a single bosonic field
\varphi
whose seed action is that of a free massless field. From the general
f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})
deformation of (
1
), we recover the usual
T\overline{T}
deformation by taking

f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})=-\frac{1}{2}\left(T^{\alpha}{}_{\beta}T^{\beta}{}_{\alpha}-(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha})^{2}\right)\,.

(15)

Evaluating a few of the terms in the perturbative expansion, we find

\displaystyle T\overline{T}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{4}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)^{2}\,,\quad T\overline{T}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)^{3}\,,

(16)

\displaystyle T\overline{T}_{2}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=-\frac{15}{16}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)^{4}\,.

This series expansion then converges to the well-known
T\overline{T}
-deformed action,

\displaystyle S^{(\lambda)}

\displaystyle=\int dtd\theta\bigg[\frac{1}{2}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)-\frac{\lambda}{4}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)^{2}

(17)

\displaystyle+\frac{\lambda^{2}}{4}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)^{3}-\frac{5\lambda^{3}}{16}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)^{4}+\cdots\bigg]

\displaystyle=\int dtd\theta\frac{1}{2\lambda}\bigg[\sqrt{1+2\lambda\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{2}+\varphi^{\prime 2}\right)}-1\bigg]\,.

T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}
Perturbative Flow for Multiple Bosons

Next we turn our attention to a deformation which was not considered in the body of this manuscript. Consider a deformation by the relevant
T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}
operator, which we define by

T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}\left(T^{\alpha}{}_{\beta}T^{\beta}{}_{\alpha}-(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha})^{2}\right)\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\,.

(18)

We will again consider a seed action for
N
massless free bosons, given in equation (
6
). The perturbative expansion for the
T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}
-deformed action takes the form

S^{(\lambda)}=S^{(0)}+\sum^{\infty}_{m=1}\frac{\lambda^{m}}{m}\int d^{2}xE~T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}_{m-1}\,,

(19)

and a few of the coefficients are

\displaystyle T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}_{0}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2^{\frac{5}{3}}}\bigg[\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\bigg]^{\frac{1}{3}}\,,

(20)

\displaystyle T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}_{1}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=\frac{-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}}{9\cdot 2^{\frac{1}{3}}\bigg[\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\bigg]^{\frac{1}{3}}}\,,

\displaystyle T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}_{2}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=-\frac{\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\right)^{2}+(\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i})^{2}+12(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime i})^{2}-14\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime j}\varphi^{\prime j}}{216\bigg[\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\bigg]}\,.

For this deformation, it does not seem possible to find an all-orders closed-form solution to the flow equation, but the perturbative
T\overline{T}^{\frac{1}{3}}
-deformed action to
\mathcal{O}\left(\lambda^{3}\right)
is

\displaystyle S^{(\lambda)}

\displaystyle=\int dt\,d\theta\,\bigg(\frac{1}{2}\left(-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}\right)

(21)

\displaystyle+\frac{\lambda}{2^{\frac{5}{3}}}\bigg[\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\bigg]^{\frac{1}{3}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\lambda^{2}}{9\cdot 2^{\frac{4}{3}}}\frac{-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}}{\bigg[\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\bigg]^{\frac{1}{3}}}

\displaystyle-\frac{\lambda^{3}}{648}\frac{\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\right)^{2}+(\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i})^{2}+12(\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime i})^{2}-14\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}\varphi^{\prime j}\varphi^{\prime j}}{\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)}+\cdots\bigg)\,.

f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})
Perturbative Flow for Multiple Bosons

To conclude this appendix, we note that one can also study the perturbative solution to the flow driven by the
f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})=f(z,x)
operator of equation (
1
) for an
arbitrary
function
f
. We again take the initial condition for the flow to be the action (
6
) for
N
free massless bosons. The first few terms in the perturbative expansion are

\displaystyle f(T\alpha{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})_{0}|_{\text{flat}}

\displaystyle=f\left(x\right)\,,\quad f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})_{1}|_{\text{flat}}=4xy\left(\frac{\partial f(x)}{\partial x}\right)^{2}\,,

(22)

where

\displaystyle x

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{i}-\varphi^{\prime i}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)\left(\dot{\varphi}^{j}+\varphi^{\prime j}\right)

(23)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(2\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\nu}\varphi^{i}\right)\left(\partial_{\nu}\varphi^{j}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{j}\right)-\left(\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{i}\right)^{2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle y

\displaystyle=-\dot{\varphi}^{i}\dot{\varphi}^{i}+\varphi^{\prime i}\varphi^{\prime i}=\partial_{\mu}\varphi^{i}\partial^{\mu}\varphi^{i}\,.

The perturbative action at
\mathcal{O}(g^{2})
is

\displaystyle S^{(g)}

\displaystyle=\int dtd\theta\bigg[\frac{y}{2}+gf\left(x\right)+2g^{2}xy\left(\frac{\partial f(x)}{\partial x}\right)^{2}+\cdots\bigg]\,.

(24)

Furthermore, to summarize in the table below, one can check equation (
24
) recovers the correct coefficients at
\mathcal{O}(g^{2})
for the perturbative actions describing
N
free massless bosons considered in this appendix.

In principle, one could also study the perturbative quantization of these more general
f(T^{\alpha}{}_{\alpha},T^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta})
-deformed scalar models. For instance, one could use the background field expansion and determine their Feynman rules as done in section
5
for the Modified Scalar theory, or study canonical quantization following section
4
.

Appendix 11.B
Details of Feynman Diagram Calculations

In this appendix, we collect the technical details of certain evaluations of Feynman diagrams which occur in the analysis of section
5
.

1
One-loop,
2
-vertex calculation

Let us first focus on the divergence structure of the diagram
\mathcal{D}_{2}
of equation (
260
), which we repeat here for convenience:

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{2}\;=\;\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\includegraphics[width=131.10168pt]{diagrams/divergent_contribution.pdf}}\;.

(25)

As we mentioned around equation (
263
), the value of this diagram can be expressed in terms of the simpler quantity

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}^{\mu\nu\rho\tau}_{2}=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\frac{(\ell+q)^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}(\ell+q)^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\ell^{2}\left(\ell+q\right)^{2}}\,.

(26)

All of the dependence on loop momenta is encoded within
{\mathcal{I}}^{\mu\nu\rho\tau}_{2}
, which we will also write as
{\mathcal{I}}_{2}
with indices suppressed for simplicity. From the value of
\mathcal{I}_{2}
, the original diagram
\mathcal{D}_{2}
is recovered from the expression (
262
), which only involves additional dependence on the classical background via the tensor
P_{\mu\nu}^{ij}
and an additional integration over the momentum
q
. Therefore, in order to study the divergences arising from the loop, it suffices to perform dimensional regularization of the quantity
\mathcal{I}_{2}
.

Expanding out the products and introducing a Feynman parameter
x
in order to resolve the denominator, we find

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}_{2}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\frac{\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\ell^{2}\left(\ell+q\right)^{2}}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\frac{\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left[\ell^{2}\left(1-x\right)+x\left(\ell+q\right)^{2}\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\frac{\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left[\ell^{2}+x\left(2\ell_{\mu}q^{\mu}+q^{2}\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\frac{\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left[\left(\ell^{\mu}+xq^{\mu}\right)^{2}+x\left(1-x\right)q^{2}\right]^{2}}\,.

(27)

In the final step, we have completed the square in the denominator by adding and subtracting
q^{2}x^{2}
. We now shift the integration variable from
\ell^{\mu}
to

\displaystyle\ell^{\prime\mu}=\ell^{\mu}-xq^{\mu}\,,

(28)

which causes the denominator to become even in
\ell^{\prime}
, and thus terms in the numerator which are odd in
\ell^{\prime\mu}
will vanish by symmetry. We immediately drop the primes on
\ell^{\prime\mu}
and write the surviving terms as

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\Bigg[\frac{\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left(\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{2}}+\frac{x^{2}\ell^{\nu}q^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}q^{\rho}}{\left(\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\left(x^{2}-2x+1\right)q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left(\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\left(x^{2}-x\right)\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}q^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}\right)}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\left(x^{4}-2x^{3}+x^{2}\right)q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}}{\left(\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{2}}\Bigg]\,

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\Bigg[\frac{\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left(\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{2}}+\frac{x^{2}\ell^{\nu}q^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}q^{\rho}}{\left(\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\left(1-x\right)^{2}q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{x\left(1-x\right)\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}+q^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\tau}q^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+\ell^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\ell^{\rho}\right)}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\left[x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}\right]q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}\Bigg]\,.

(29)

By a symmetry argument similar to the one discussed around equations (
256
) and (
258
), within the integral we can replace products of loop momenta with symmetrized combinations of metric tensors:

\displaystyle\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\nu}

\displaystyle\to\frac{1}{d}\ell^{2}g^{\mu\nu}\,,

\displaystyle\ell^{\mu}\ell^{\nu}\ell^{\rho}\ell^{\tau}

\displaystyle\to\frac{1}{d\left(d+2\right)}\ell^{4}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)\,.

(30)

Applying the replacements (
30
), the integral
{\mathcal{I}}_{2}
becomes

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\Bigg(\frac{\ell^{4}}{d\left(d+2\right)}\frac{g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\ell^{2}}{d}\frac{x^{2}g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\ell^{2}}{d}\frac{\left(1-x\right)^{2}g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\ell^{2}}{d}\frac{x\left(1-x\right)\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle\qquad+\frac{x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}}{\left[\ell^{2}+q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{2}}\Bigg)\,.

(31)

It will be convenient to make use of the standard result

\displaystyle\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\frac{\ell^{2\beta}}{\left(\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2}\right)^{\alpha}}=i\left(-1\right)^{\alpha+\beta}\frac{\Gamma\left(\beta+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(\alpha-\beta-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(\alpha\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Delta^{2\left(\frac{d}{2}-\alpha+\beta\right)}\,,

(32)

which can be found, for instance, in equation (A.4) in
[
375
]
. Using (
32
) with

\displaystyle\Delta^{2}=-q^{2}x\left(1-x\right)

(33)

in equation (
31
), we find

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}

\displaystyle=\frac{i}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(2\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\Bigg(\frac{\Delta^{d}\Gamma\left(2+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d\left(d+2\right)}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)

\displaystyle+\frac{\Delta^{d-2}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}x\left(1-x\right)\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)

\displaystyle+\frac{\Delta^{d-2}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}x^{2}g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Delta^{d-2}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}\left(1-x\right)^{2}g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}

\displaystyle+\Delta^{d-4}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(2-\frac{d}{2}\right)\left[x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}\right]q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}\Bigg)\,.

(34)

Using gamma function identities and some algebra, one can simplify this to

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}

\displaystyle=\frac{i\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\Bigg(\frac{\Delta^{d}}{4}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)-\frac{d\Delta^{d-2}}{4}x^{2}g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}

\displaystyle-\frac{d\Delta^{d-2}}{4}\left(1-x\right)^{2}g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}

\displaystyle-\frac{d\Delta^{d-2}}{4}x\left(1-x\right)\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)

\displaystyle+\frac{d\left(d-2\right)\Delta^{d-4}}{4}x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}\Bigg)\,.

(35)

After substituting in for
\Delta^{2}
using the definition (
33
), we can now evaluate the resulting integrals using the formula

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}xx^{\alpha-1}\left(1-x\right)^{\beta-1}

\displaystyle=\frac{\Gamma\left(\alpha\right)\Gamma\left(\beta\right)}{\Gamma\left(\alpha+\beta\right)}=\mathrm{B}(\alpha,\beta)\,,

(36)

which we recognize as the definition of the beta function
\mathrm{B}(\alpha,\beta)
. By doing this, we find

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}=\frac{i\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{4\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}}\int_{0}^{1}d^{d}x\Bigg(

\displaystyle d\left(d-2\right)q^{d-4}\left[-x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{\frac{d}{2}}q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}-dq^{d-2}\left(-x\right)^{\frac{d}{2}-1}\left(1-x\right)^{\frac{d}{2}+1}g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}

\displaystyle+q^{d}\left[-x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{\frac{d}{2}}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)

\displaystyle-dq^{d-2}\left[\left(-x\right)^{\frac{d}{2}+1}\left(1-x\right)^{\frac{d}{2}-1}\right]g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}

\displaystyle+dq^{d-2}\left[-x\left(1-x\right)\right]^{\frac{d}{2}}\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)\Bigg)

\displaystyle=\frac{i\left(-1\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{4\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}}\Bigg(q^{d}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}}{\Gamma\left(d+2\right)}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)

\displaystyle+dq^{d-2}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+2\right)}{\Gamma\left(d+2\right)}\left[g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}+g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}\right]+d\left(d-2\right)q^{d-4}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}}{\Gamma\left(d+2\right)}q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}

\displaystyle+dq^{d-2}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}}{\Gamma\left(d+2\right)}\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)\Bigg)\,.

(37)

Note that each term in (
37
) scales as
q^{d}
, as expected. Factoring out the gamma functions, we have found

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}

\displaystyle=\frac{i\left(-1\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{4\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}}{\Gamma\left(d+2\right)}\Bigg[q^{d}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)

\displaystyle+d\left(d-2\right)q^{d-4}q^{\nu}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+dq^{d-2}\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)

\displaystyle+\left(d+2\right)q^{d-2}\left(g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}+g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}\right)\Bigg]\,.

(38)

Finally, to perform dimensional regularization, we set the spacetime dimension to
d=2+2\epsilon
and take
\epsilon\to 0
using the limiting behavior

\displaystyle\Gamma\left(-1-\epsilon\right)=\frac{1}{\epsilon}-\gamma+1+\mathcal{O}\left(\epsilon\right)

(39)

for the gamma functions. Keeping only divergent terms, we arrive at the final expression

\displaystyle{\mathcal{I}}_{2}

\displaystyle=\left(\frac{1}{\epsilon}\right)\frac{-i}{24\left(4\pi\right)}\bigg[q^{2}\left(g^{\mu\nu}g^{\rho\tau}+g^{\mu\rho}g^{\nu\tau}+g^{\mu\tau}g^{\nu\rho}\right)

\displaystyle+2\left(q^{\nu}q^{\mu}g^{\tau\rho}+g^{\mu\tau}q^{\nu}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\mu}q^{\tau}q^{\rho}+g^{\nu\rho}q^{\mu}q^{\tau}\right)

\displaystyle+4\left(g^{\mu\rho}q^{\nu}q^{\tau}+g^{\nu\tau}q^{\mu}q^{\rho}\right)\bigg]\,.

(40)

This completes the evaluation of the divergent contribution from
{\mathcal{I}}_{2}
, which justifies the result (
264
) which was quoted in the body of the paper.

2
One-loop,
n
-vertex calculation

The
n
-vertex diagram
\mathcal{D}_{n}
can be computed via a generalization of the method used in appendix
1
. We again write
\ell
for the loop momentum and we label the external momenta as
q_{i}
, for
i=0,\ldots,n-1
, with momentum conservation implying that

\displaystyle q_{n-1}=-\sum_{i=0}^{n-2}q_{i}\,.

(41)

As we did with
\mathcal{D}_{2}
in equation (
261
), let us strip off various factors of
P_{\mu\nu}{}^{ij}
to write

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{n}

\displaystyle=\left(-2\tanh(\gamma)\right)^{N}

\displaystyle\cdot\int\left(\frac{d^{d}q_{0}}{(2\pi)^{d}}P_{(\mu_{1}\mu_{2})}^{i_{1}i_{2}}(q_{0})\right)\left(\frac{d^{d}q_{0}}{(2\pi)^{d}}P_{(\mu_{3}\mu_{4})}^{i_{2}i_{3}}(q_{1})\right)\cdots\left(\frac{d^{d}q_{n-2}}{(2\pi)^{d}}P_{(\mu_{2n-3}\mu_{2n-2})}^{i_{n-1}i_{n}}(q_{n-2})\right)

\displaystyle\cdot P_{(\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n})}^{i_{n}i_{1}}(q_{n-1})\left({\mathcal{I}}_{n}\right)^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}\,,

(42)

where
{\mathcal{I}}_{n}
is the simpler integral

\displaystyle\left({\mathcal{I}}_{n}\right)^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{(2\pi)^{d}}\,\left(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{-2}\right)\left(\prod_{k=1}^{n}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q_{j}\right)^{\mu_{2k-1}}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q_{j}\right)^{\mu_{2k}}\right)\,.

(43)

We will further break up
\mathcal{I}_{n}
into pieces and evaluate each piece in turn. Let us write the integrand of (
43
) as a product

\displaystyle\left({\mathcal{I}}_{n}\right)^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{(2\pi)^{d}}\,\mathcal{P}_{n}\mathcal{V}^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}\,,

(44)

where the symbol

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{n}

\displaystyle=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{-2}

(45)

refers to the collection of all factors in
\mathcal{I}_{n}
which come from propagators, and the symbol

\displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q_{j}\right)^{\mu_{2k-1}}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q_{j}\right)^{\mu_{2k}}\,,

(46)

which we will sometimes abbreviate as
\mathcal{V}
, refers to the pieces coming from vertex factors.

In order to highlight the divergence structure of the diagram
\mathcal{D}_{n}
, we will focus on performing the loop momentum integral of various terms appearing in the product
\mathcal{P}\mathcal{V}
of equation (
44
), and neglect the additional structure arising from the contraction with the various tensors
P_{\mu\nu}^{ij}
to obtain
\mathcal{D}_{n}
in (
42
).

Let us begin by simplifying the product
\mathcal{P}
of
n
propagator factors. In general, we can write the product of
n
propagators using a Feynman parameterization:

\displaystyle\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}A_{i}^{-1}

\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{1}\left(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}d^{d}x_{i}\right)\delta\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_{i}-1\right)\frac{\left(n-1\right)!}{\left[\sum_{i}x_{i}A_{i}\right]^{n}}\,.

(47)

The product of propagators inside the loop can thus be expressed as

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}=\int_{0}^{1}\left(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}d^{d}x_{i}\right)\delta\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_{i}-1\right)\left[\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_{i}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\right]^{-n}\,.

(48)

As
\sum_{i}x_{i}=1
, we can expand and reduce the square bracketed term to

\displaystyle\left[\sum_{i}x_{i}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\right]^{-n}

\displaystyle=\left[\ell^{2}+\sum_{i}x_{i}\left(2\ell_{\mu}\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}^{\mu}+\left(\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\right)\right]^{-n}

\displaystyle=\left[\left(\ell+\sum_{i}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}-\left(\sum_{i}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}+\sum_{i}x_{i}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\right]^{-n}\,.

(49)

We change variables in the loop momentum by shifting

\displaystyle\ell^{\mu}\to\ell^{\mu}-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q^{\mu}_{j}\,,

(50)

so that the bracketed expression becomes

\displaystyle\left[\sum_{i}x_{i}\left(\ell+\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\right]^{-n}

\displaystyle=\left[\ell^{2}-\left(\sum_{i}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}+\sum_{i}x_{i}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\right]^{-n}

\displaystyle=\left[\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2}\right]^{-n}\,,

(51)

where we have defined

\displaystyle\Delta^{2}

\displaystyle=\left(\sum_{i}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}-\sum_{i}x_{i}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{i}q_{j}\right)^{2}\,.

(52)

Overall this allows us to write the propagators as

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}=(n-1)!\int_{0}^{1}\left(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}d^{d}x_{i}\right)\delta\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_{i}-1\right)\left(\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2}\right)^{-n}\,.

(53)

Next let us turn to the contributions from the vertices in equation (
46
), which yield factors of momenta in the numerator of the integrand. Under the change of variables (
50
) which renders the denominator of
\mathcal{P}
quadratic in
\ell
, the vertex factor contribution becomes

\displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\left(\ell-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q_{j}\right)^{\mu_{2k-1}}\left(\ell-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q_{j}\right)^{\mu_{2k}}\,.

(54)

We expand this product in descending powers of
\ell
as only powers
\ell^{2n}
and
\ell^{2n-2}
will lead to divergent terms. We have that

\displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\ell^{\mu_{2k-1}}\ell^{\mu_{2k}}+\sum_{a=1}^{2n}\sum_{b>a}^{2n}\left(\prod_{c\neq a,b}^{2n}\ell^{\mu_{c}}\right)f^{\mu_{a}}\left(x,q,a\right)f^{\mu_{b}}\left(x,q,b\right)+\mathcal{O}\left(\ell^{2n-4}\right)\,,

(55)

where we have defined for brevity

\displaystyle f^{\mu}\left(x,q,a\right)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{j=0}^{i}x_{i}q_{j}^{\mu}+\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor\frac{a-1}{2}\rfloor}q_{j}^{\mu}\,.

(56)

Next we will replace products of loop momenta using the generalized symmetrization rule of equation (
258
). To ease notation, let us write

\displaystyle g^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{n}}=g^{(\mu_{1}\mu_{2}}\cdots g^{\mu_{n-1}\mu_{n})}\,

(57)

for the symmetrized combination of derivatives appearing in this expression. When no confusion is possible, we will also write
g^{\{\mu\}}
for (
57
), where
\{\mu\}
