is understood to refer to a multi-index
\{\mu\}=\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{n}
. With this notation, the replacement rule becomes

\displaystyle\prod_{i=1}^{n}\ell^{\mu_{2i-1}}\ell^{\mu_{2i}}\to\frac{\ell^{2n}\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-2+2n\right)!!}g^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}\,.

(58)

This transforms the vertex factor contribution to

\displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n-1}\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle=\frac{\ell^{2n}\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-2+2n\right)!!}g^{\mu_{1}\cdots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle\quad+\frac{\ell^{2n-2}\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-4+2n\right)!!}\sum_{a=1}^{2n}\sum_{b>a}^{2n}g^{\{\mu\neq\mu_{a},\mu_{b}\}}f^{\mu_{a}}\left(x,q,a\right)f^{\mu_{b}}\left(x,q,b\right)+\mathcal{O}\left(\ell^{2n-4}\right)\,.

(59)

In equation (
59
), we have written
g^{\{\mu\neq\mu_{a},\mu_{b}\}}
to refer to a product of the form (
57
) in which the multi-index
\{\mu\}
runs over all possible values except for the two indices
\mu_{a}
and
\mu_{b}
, which are excluded.

Let us now combine the pieces and identify the divergent terms in
\mathcal{D}_{n}
. We can evaluate

\displaystyle\left({\mathcal{I}}_{n}\right)^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle\quad=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{(2\pi)^{d}}\mathcal{P}\mathcal{V}^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n}}\,

\displaystyle\quad=\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{(2\pi)^{d}}\left(n-1\right)!\int_{0}^{1}\left(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}d^{d}x_{i}\right)\delta\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_{i}-1\right)\left(\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2}\right)^{-n}

\displaystyle\cdot\Bigg(\frac{\ell^{2n}\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-2+2n\right)!!}g^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}+\frac{\ell^{2n-2}\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-4+2n\right)!!}\sum_{a=1}^{2n}\sum_{b>a}^{2n}g^{\{\mu\neq\mu_{a},\mu_{b}\}}f^{\mu_{a}}\left(x,q,a\right)f^{\mu_{b}}\left(x,q,b\right)

\displaystyle+\mathcal{O}\left(\ell^{2n-4}\right)\Bigg)\,,

(60)

in terms of the known integral

\displaystyle\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\frac{\ell^{2\beta}}{\left(\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2}\right)^{\alpha}}

\displaystyle=i\left(-1\right)^{\alpha+\beta}\frac{\Gamma\left(\beta+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(\alpha-\beta-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(\alpha\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Delta^{2\left(\frac{d}{2}-\alpha+\beta\right)}\,.

(61)

First let us justify why the terms of order
\ell^{2n-4}
and lower in equation (
60
) will not give divergent contributions. A term proportional to
\ell^{2n-4}
in the parentheses of (
60
), after multiplying the propagator factor
(\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2})^{-n}
, gives a term in the integrand of the form (
61
) with
\alpha=n
and
\beta=n-2
. Such a term gives a contribution

\displaystyle\int\frac{d^{d}\ell}{\left(2\pi\right)^{d}}\frac{\ell^{2(n-2)}}{\left(\ell^{2}-\Delta^{2}\right)^{n}}

\displaystyle=i\left(-1\right)^{n+(n-2)}\frac{\Gamma\left(n-2+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(2-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(n\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Delta^{2\left(\frac{d}{2}-n+(n-2)\right)}\,.

(62)

In the limit as
d\to 2
, the two factors of gamma functions in the numerator of (
62
) tend to
\Gamma(n-1)
and
\Gamma(1)
, which are both finite since
n>2
. Since we are only interested in computing the divergent contributions arising from these diagrams, we ignore these terms. Similarly, any terms of lower order in
\ell
can be evaluated in the same way but with even smaller values of
\beta
, which also lead to finite contributions from the gamma functions.

Let us therefore focus on the divergent terms. The term in the integrand proportional to
\ell^{2n}
in equation (
60
) takes the form (
61
) with
\alpha=\beta=n
. Similarly, the term in the integrand that scales as
\ell^{2n-2}
is of the form (
61
) with
\alpha=n
and
\beta=n-1
. Evaluating the loop momentum integrals then gives

\displaystyle\left({\mathcal{I}}_{n}\right)^{\mu_{1}\mu_{2}\ldots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle=\left(n-1\right)!\int_{0}^{1}\left(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}dx_{i}\right)\delta\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_{i}-1\right)

\displaystyle\quad\cdot\Bigg(\frac{i\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-2+2n\right)!!}g^{\mu_{1}\cdots\mu_{2n}}\frac{\Gamma\left(n+\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(n\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d}

\displaystyle\quad+\frac{i\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-4+2n\right)!!}\sum_{a=1}^{2n}\sum_{b>a}^{2n}g^{\{\mu\neq\mu_{a},\mu_{b}\}}f^{\mu_{a}}\left(x,q,a\right)f^{\mu_{b}}\left(x,q,b\right)

\displaystyle\quad\cdot\frac{\Gamma\left(n-1+\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(n\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-2}\Bigg)\,.

(63)

To better analyze the divergence structure, it is useful to define shorthand notation for the two terms appearing in (
63
), which we call
\mathbf{C}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
and
\mathbf{D}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
:

\displaystyle\mathbf{C}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle\equiv\frac{i\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-2+2n\right)!!}g^{\mu_{1}\cdots\mu_{2n}}\frac{\Gamma\left(n+\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(n\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d}\,\,

\displaystyle\mathbf{D}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle\equiv\frac{i\left(d-2\right)!!}{\left(d-4+2n\right)!!}\sum_{a=1}^{2n}\sum_{b>a}^{2n}g^{\{\mu\neq\mu_{a},\mu_{b}\}}f^{\mu_{a}}\left(x,q,a\right)f^{\mu_{b}}\left(x,q,b\right)

\displaystyle\qquad\cdot\frac{\Gamma\left(n-1+\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(n\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-2}\,.

(64)

Both contributions
\mathbf{C}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
and
\mathbf{D}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
scale as
q^{d}
and contain a polynomial in
x_{i}
of degree
d
. In
\mathbf{C}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
, this
q^{d}
dependence is contained within
\Delta^{d}
, and for
\mathbf{D}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
, the power of
q^{d-2}
from
\Delta^{d-2}
is compensated by two factors of
q
, one of which sits in each function
f^{\mu}
.

Therefore, we conclude that in the limit
d\to 2
, all such
n
vertex diagrams have the same general structure as the
2
-vertex diagram which we saw in (
40
). In particular, both
\mathbf{C}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
and
\mathbf{D}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}
generate divergences of the form
\frac{1}{\epsilon}
because they are proportional to
\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)
and
\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)
, respectively.

We conclude that

\displaystyle\mathbf{C}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle\sim\frac{1}{\epsilon}q^{2}g^{\mu_{1}\cdots\mu_{2n}}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbf{D}_{2n}^{\mu_{1}\ldots\mu_{2n}}

\displaystyle\sim\frac{1}{\epsilon}\sum_{a=1}^{2n}\sum_{b>a}^{2n}q^{\mu_{a}}q^{\mu_{b}}g^{\{\mu\neq\mu_{a},\mu_{b}\}}\,.

(65)

3
m
-loop, two-vertex calculation

In this appendix, we will show how to evaluate the integral over one of the
m
loop momenta
\ell_{i}
which appear in the expression for the two-vertex,
m
-loop diagram of equation (
268
). It suffices to integrate over the final momentum
\ell_{m}
, since the result may then be iterated to evaluate the other
m-1
integrals.

Therefore, let us focus on performing the integration over
\ell_{m}
in the quantity
\mathfrak{L}_{m,2}
of equation (
274
). Specifically, we will compute the quantity

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}\frac{\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\nu_{m}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\tau_{m}}}{\ell_{m}^{2}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{2}}\,.

(66)

This object
L_{m,2}
is proportional to the remaining integrand that one finds by performing the integral over
\ell_{m}
in the definition of
\mathfrak{L}_{m,2}
. As we will see, after obtaining an expression for
L_{m,2}
, this result can be used recursively to evaluate
\mathfrak{L}_{m,2}
itself.

We notice the integral in equation (
66
) is exactly of the form of the one appearing in the
1
-loop,
2
-vertex diagram which we evaluated in appendix
1
. Proceeding in the same way, we introduce a Feynman parameter
x
to write

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}dx\frac{\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\nu_{m}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m}^{2}+x\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{2}\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}dx\frac{\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\nu_{m}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell_{m}^{2}+x\left(2\ell_{m}\cdot\ell_{m-1}-\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right)\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}dx\frac{\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\nu_{m}}\left(\ell_{m}-\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\left(\ell_{m}+x\ell_{m-1}\right)^{2}-x^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{2}+x\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}\,,

(67)

or after shifting the integration variable as
\ell_{m}\to\ell_{m}-x\ell_{m-1}
,

\displaystyle L_{m,2}=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}dx

\displaystyle\frac{\left(\ell_{m}-x\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\nu_{m+1}}\left(\ell_{m}-x\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\tau_{m+1}}\left(\ell_{m}-\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\nu_{m}}\left(\ell_{m}-\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}\right)^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell_{m}^{2}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}\,.

(68)

We may keep only even powers of
\ell_{m}
in the integrand, as odd powers vanish by symmetry:

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}dx\Bigg(\frac{\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m}}+x^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m}}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell_{m}^{2}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}

(69)

\displaystyle+\frac{x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m}}+\left(1-x\right)^{2}\ell_{m}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell^{2}_{m}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell^{2}_{m}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}\Bigg)\,.

We now replace products of
\ell_{m}^{\mu}
with powers of
\ell_{m}
and symmetrized metric factors, following the generalized symmetrization rule (
258
), which yields

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\int d^{d}\ell_{m}dx\Bigg(\frac{\frac{\ell_{m}^{4}}{d\left(d+2\right)}g^{(\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}g^{\nu_{m}\tau_{m})}+x^{2}\frac{\ell_{m}^{2}}{d}g^{\mu_{m}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}}{\left[\ell_{m}^{2}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{x\left(1-x\right)\frac{\ell_{m}^{2}}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell_{m}^{2}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{x\left(1-x\right)\frac{\ell_{m}^{2}}{d}g^{\tau_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}+\left(1-x\right)^{2}\frac{\ell_{m}^{2}}{d}g^{{\nu_{m+1}}{\tau_{m+1}}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell^{2}_{m}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}

\displaystyle+\frac{x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}}{\left[\ell^{2}_{m}+x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\right]^{2}}\Bigg)\,.

(70)

Splitting the numerator up, we can once again apply the standard formula (
61
) with

\displaystyle\Delta^{2}=-x\left(1-x\right)\ell_{m-1}^{2}\,,

(71)

which gives

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\frac{i}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\int_{0}^{1}dx\Bigg(\frac{1}{d\left(d+2\right)}g^{(\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}g^{\nu_{m}\tau_{m})}\Gamma\left(2+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d}

\displaystyle+\frac{x^{2}}{d}g^{\mu_{m}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\frac{x\left(1-x\right)}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\frac{x\left(1-x\right)}{d}g^{\tau_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\frac{\left(1-x\right)^{2}}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-2}

\displaystyle+x^{2}\left(1-x\right)^{2}\ell_{n-2}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(2-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Delta^{d-4}\Bigg)\,.

(72)

Replacing
\Delta
using its definition in equation (
71
), we see that each term contains
d
overall factors of loop momenta:

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\frac{i}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}\int_{0}^{1}dx\Bigg(\frac{\Gamma\left(2+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d\left(d+2\right)}g^{(\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}g^{\nu_{m}\tau_{m})}\left(x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\ell_{m-1}^{d}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\mu_{m}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}x^{\frac{d}{2}+1}\left(1-x\right)^{\frac{d}{2}-1}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\left(x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\tau_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\left(x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Gamma\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}x^{\frac{d}{2}-1}\left(1-x\right)^{\frac{d}{2}+1}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle+\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(2-\frac{d}{2}\right)\left(x\left(1-x\right)\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-4}\Bigg)\,.

(73)

We now use the identity
\Gamma\left(1+x\right)=x\Gamma\left(x\right)
to factor and cancel the gamma functions, and finally evaluate the Feynman integrals, giving the result

\displaystyle L_{m,2}

\displaystyle=\frac{i\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\left(4\pi\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(d+2\right)}\Bigg(\frac{\left(1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\frac{d}{2}}{d\left(d+2\right)}g^{(\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}g^{\nu_{m}\tau_{m})}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{d}

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\mu_{m}\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+2\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{\frac{d}{2}\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{\frac{d}{2}\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\tau_{m+1}\nu_{m}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{\frac{d}{2}\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)}{d}g^{\nu_{m+1}\tau_{m+1}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+2\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-2}

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad+\left(1-\frac{d}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}+1\right)^{2}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m+1}}\ell_{m-1}^{\nu_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{\tau_{m}}\ell_{m-1}^{d-4}\Bigg)\,.

(74)

We see that all terms scale as
\ell_{m-1}^{d}
and the only divergent gamma function is
\Gamma\left(-\frac{d}{2}\right)
. This establishes the result used in the body of section
5
, in the text above equation (
276
), which can then be applied iteratively to evaluate the remaining loop integrals.
